subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Geographers classify islands according to how they were geologically formed.
• The three primary origin categories are volcanic, coral, and continental.
• Iceland is a volcanic island, formed by magma rising from the seafloor.
• The Maldives are coral islands, built up from the skeletons of marine organisms.
• Madagascar is a continental island, separated from a larger landmass millions of years ago.
• About 90% of the world's islands are classified as either volcanic or continental.
prompt: The student wants to make a generalization about how islands are geologically formed. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Geological origin is one of the features by which geographers classify and compare the world's islands.
choices.B: Geographers study and compare how islands around the world were geologically formed.
choices.C: The three primary categories that describe how islands were geologically formed are volcanic, coral, and continental.
choices.D: Most islands in the world were formed either by volcanic activity or by separation from a larger continental landmass.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer. The sentence makes a generalization about how islands are geologically formed by stating that most islands were formed either by volcanic activity or by separation from a larger continental landmass. This generalization is supported by the note that about 90% of the world's islands are classified as either volcanic or continental, along with the notes defining these two categories.
